channel.title: GoodsInfinite Pet — Care Journal
channel.description: Vet-informed dog & cat care guides and answers.

item.title: Cat Stud Tail: Why the Tail Base Gets Greasy and Bald
item.description: A greasy, bald patch at the base of your cat's tail is stud tail, an overactive tail gland. See how to clean it, what really helps, and when it needs a vet.

item.title: Crate Training a Puppy: A Calm Plan That Actually Works
item.description: Crate training a puppy works when the crate is never a punishment. Here is a day-by-day plan, realistic bladder limits by age, and how to handle night crying.

item.title: Swollen Eye in Dogs: Causes and When It Is an Emergency
item.description: A puffy eye in a dog is often an allergy or a sting, but glaucoma and abscesses look similar. Learn the signs that mean same-day vet care, and safe first aid.

item.title: Cat Squinting One Eye: Causes and When It Is an Emergency
item.description: A cat squinting one eye is usually in pain, not sleepy. See the eight common causes, which ones threaten the eye, and what to do before the vet visit.

item.title: Cat Nail Cut Too Short: How to Stop the Bleeding Fast
item.description: Cut into the quick? Here is how to stop a cat nail bleeding fast, what to put on it, what never to use, and when the toe needs a vet instead of home care.

item.title: Dog Scared of Strangers: A Step-by-Step Confidence Plan
item.description: A dog who barks or cowers at visitors is frightened, not dominant. Here is a four-stage plan that lowers fear without force, plus signs a vet is needed.

item.title: Cat Hyperesthesia: Why Your Cat's Back Ripples and Twitches
item.description: Feline hyperesthesia makes a cat's back ripple and triggers tail chasing and biting. Learn the triggers, the lookalikes vets rule out and what really helps.

item.title: Matted Cat Fur: How to Untangle It Without a Fight
item.description: Matted cat fur is not just cosmetic - it can signal arthritis or dental pain. Learn how to untangle loose mats safely and when clipping is the kinder choice.

item.title: How to Remove Tartar From a Dog's Teeth (What Works)
item.description: Hard tartar cannot be dissolved at home, but you can stop it coming back. What really removes dog tartar, what wastes your money, and how to slow it down.

item.title: Cat Flea Allergy: Why One Flea Causes So Much Itching
item.description: Cat flea allergy is a reaction to flea saliva, so one bite can mean weeks of scratching. Learn the signs, the paper test and a plan that actually works.

item.title: Cat Not Eating: When to Worry and What to Try First
item.description: A cat that stops eating can develop fatty liver in as little as three days. Learn the real causes, safe home tricks and when the 24-hour rule applies.

item.title: Dog Corneal Ulcer: Signs, Causes and Why It Is Urgent
item.description: A dog eye ulcer is a scratch on the cornea that can worsen within hours. Spot the warning signs, avoid the drops that make it worse, and know when to go now.

item.title: Cat Ringworm: Signs, Treatment and How to Stop the Spread
item.description: Cat ringworm is a contagious fungal skin infection, not a worm, and people can catch it. Learn the signs, how vets confirm it, and how to clear it for good.

item.title: Cat Tooth Resorption: Why Cats Lose Teeth and What Helps
item.description: Cat tooth resorption is the top cause of tooth loss in cats, and it hurts even when your cat still eats. Learn the signs, the types and what treatment helps.

item.title: Dog Fainting: Why It Happens and When It Is an Emergency
item.description: Dog fainting is usually a brief collapse from a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain. Learn how to tell it from a seizure and when it needs urgent care.

item.title: Cat Skin Allergies: Why Your Cat Is Itchy and What Helps
item.description: Cat skin allergies cause constant itching, scabs and hair loss. Learn the common triggers, how vets test for them, and what actually calms irritated skin.

item.title: Dog Diarrhoea: Common Causes and When to Call a Vet
item.description: Dog diarrhoea is usually short-lived, but some causes are urgent. Learn the common triggers, what to feed during recovery, and the red flags for a vet visit.

item.title: Dog Gingivitis: Early Signs and Home Care That Works
item.description: Dog gingivitis is red, swollen gums that are reversible early and painful later. Learn the warning signs, a home routine that helps, and when to see a vet.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Meow at Night? Causes and Calm Nights
item.description: Cat meowing at night is usually hunger, boredom or a medical problem in older cats. Learn what is normal, what needs a vet, and how to quiet the chorus.

item.title: How to Check Your Dog's Weight and Body Condition at Home
item.description: Body condition score beats the scale for spotting weight problems early. Learn a one-minute rib, waist and belly check plus how to weigh your dog at home.

item.title: How to Give Your Dog or Cat Eye Drops Without a Fight
item.description: Eye drops only work if they land in the eye. Learn the lower-lid pocket technique, how to handle a pet who fights it, and the mistakes that waste a dose.

item.title: Cat Hair Loss: Common Causes and When to Worry About It
item.description: Cat hair loss usually means fleas, over-grooming, ringworm or allergies. Learn normal shedding vs real alopecia and when symmetrical bald patches need a vet.

item.title: Cat Stomatitis: Why Your Cat's Mouth Hurts and What Helps
item.description: Feline stomatitis is severe mouth inflammation that makes eating painful. Learn the signs, why it happens and how vets treat it, plus when to book an exam.

item.title: Dog Coughing: 7 Common Causes and When to Call a Vet
item.description: A dog cough is usually kennel cough or a collapsing trachea, but heart disease and pneumonia look similar. Learn the 7 common causes plus the red flags.

item.title: Cat Scratching Furniture: How to Redirect Without Punishment
item.description: Scratching is normal cat behaviour, not revenge. Redirect it to the right post in two weeks, protect your sofa, and learn why declawing is never the answer.

item.title: Cat Watery Eye: Causes, Discharge & When to See a Vet
item.description: A watery cat eye is usually tear overflow, not crying. Learn what clear, sticky and yellow discharge each mean, and when a squinting eye needs a same-day vet.

item.title: Senior Dog Care: What Changes After Age 7 and How to Help
item.description: Dogs turn senior at 7 to 10 depending on their size. Here is what to change: twice-yearly check-ups, home mobility checks and small home edits that help.

item.title: Dog Food Allergies: Signs, Itchy Skin & How to Find Triggers
item.description: Itchy, year-round skin and ear infections can point to a food allergy. Learn the signs, the 8-week elimination diet that confirms it, and when to see a vet.

item.title: Heatstroke in Dogs: Signs, First Aid & When to Call a Vet
item.description: Heatstroke in dogs is a fast-moving emergency. Learn the early warning signs, how to cool a dog safely in the first ten minutes, and when to call the vet.

item.title: Professional Dog Dental Cleaning: How Often Is It Needed?
item.description: Most dogs need a professional dental cleaning under anaesthesia every 1 to 3 years. Here is what the vet actually does, and how to stretch the interval safely.

item.title: Cherry Eye in Dogs: Causes and When to Take Action
item.description: Cherry eye is a prolapsed tear gland, not a tumour. Learn which dogs get it, what genuinely helps at home, and when the eye needs surgery or same-day care.

item.title: How Much Water Should a Dog Drink? A Daily Hydration Guide
item.description: How much water a dog needs per day, how to measure your own dog's normal, the signs of dehydration, and when a change in drinking means see the vet today.

item.title: How to Clean Cat Ears Safely: A Calm Step-by-Step Method
item.description: Cat ears usually need far less cleaning than owners think. Here is a calm, safe method, what a healthy ear looks like, and the signs that mean see a vet first.

item.title: Cat Peeing Outside the Litter Box: Causes and Fixes
item.description: Peeing outside the box is a message, not spite. Learn how to rule out medical causes with a vet, fix the setup, and stop the spot smelling like a toilet.

item.title: Broken Tooth in Dogs: What to Do and When It's Urgent
item.description: A cracked or chipped dog tooth can expose the pulp and infect the root within days. Learn the signs, safe first aid, and when it is a same-day vet visit.

item.title: Why Is My Dog Not Eating? Causes and When to Call a Vet

item.title: Why Does My Dog Smell? 6 Causes and How to Fix It Fast
